— I — Provenance
The Gate · 1916
Built in 1916.
Named by Walter Hines Page.
The gate has been open since 1916.
Walter Hines Page · 1855–1918
He named it
Garran Hill.
The life he imagined
happened elsewhere.

Page bought the land in February 1913, sailed for London weeks later, and watched the house rise from three thousand miles away. President Wilson had offered him the ambassadorship to the Court of St. James's -- he accepted and left before the foundation was poured.

When he finally returned to Pinehurst in December 1918, he stayed at Currituck Cottage -- not Garran Hill -- and died there ten days later.

The house was built for a life he never had the chance to live.

"Well, Frank, I did get here after all, didn't I?" — Walter Hines Page, Aberdeen station, December 11, 1918
